requirement:
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.authoring.search_accounting.excerpts`.

**Obligations derived from the text**
1. Matching and context excerpts from both `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` must stay inside the source span of the item named by `file` and `item`.
2. That span includes the item's attached source: its doc comments, attributes and attached comments, per `requirements.references.outline_comments`.
3. Clipping must also apply inside a physical line that holds several items.

I read `src/authoring/tools.rs#impl[SearchNodes]/fn[entries]` only to see how the code is structured. Both tools go through that one function, which clips each line to the node's source span plus its owned comments.

**Test mapping**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_excerpts_stop_at_byte_boundaries_including_attached_comments_and_attributes]` runs both `ripgrep` (context 99) and `ast_grep` over one Rust file. The file holds adjacent functions, a doc comment plus `#[inline]` before `fn target`, and a shared line with `fn left`, a trailing block comment, `#[inline] fn right` and `fn last`.
  - **Span clipping:** it asserts exactly three matches, with items `fn[target]`, `fn[left]` and `fn[right]`. The large context would pull in neighbouring lines if clipping failed. The test asserts that `unwanted_before`, `unwanted_after`, `unwanted_last` and `fn last` never appear in the output.
  - **Attached source:** for `ripgrep` it asserts that `fn[target]`'s lines contain `needle docs` and `#[inline]`. For both tools it asserts that `fn[left]`'s lines contain `needle attached`, and that `fn[right]`'s lines contain `#[inline] fn right`.
  - **Shared-line clipping:** `fn[left]`'s excerpt must not contain `fn right`. `fn[right]`'s excerpt must contain neither `fn left` nor `needle attached`.
  - **Non-ASCII and redaction:** a multibyte `café` plus a token on the same line check byte-boundary slicing. The token must not appear unredacted.
  - **Context 0:** two follow-up `ripgrep` queries with context 0 confirm that `café` yields only `fn[target]` and that `inline` yields `fn[target]` and `fn[right]`. The second shows attribute lines are attributed to the right items.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[exact_match_ranges_preserve_regex_anchors_and_skip_unmatched_or_binary_sources]` asserts that the whole-line excerpt `fn exact() { needle(); }` is returned unchanged and not extended into following items despite context 10. It uses anchored and case-insensitive regexes.

**Gaps considered**
- Clipping logic is language-agnostic, so other languages need no separate test.
- `ast_grep` excerpts are checked through the same function and the same file, including the shared-line case.
- I found no plausible violating behaviour that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} search_accounting.excerpts
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
